scope_note: Peer-reviewed experiments, critiques, consensus reviews, expert assessments, and current syntheses.

sources.title: Information transmission under conditions of sensory shielding
sources.authors_or_owner: Russell Targ and Harold Puthoff; Nature
sources.stance_or_result: Reports experiments interpreted by the authors as evidence of information transfer under sensory shielding.
sources.limitations: Early small-sample work; later critics challenged controls, judging, and reproducibility. Read with the replies and critiques.
sources.rights_note: Publisher-owned scholarly article. Link by DOI; do not republish the article text.

sources.title: A Perceptual Channel for Information Transfer over Kilometer Distances: Historical Perspective and Recent Research
sources.authors_or_owner: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ; Proceedings of the IEEE
sources.stance_or_result: Presents the authors' historical and experimental case for anomalous remote information transfer over distance.
sources.limitations: Combines review and advocacy with experimental reporting; independent replication and protocol criticism must be evaluated separately.
sources.rights_note: Use the NASA bibliographic locator and publisher record; do not assume unrestricted rights to the published article.

sources.title: Information transmission in remote viewing experiments
sources.authors_or_owner: David Marks and Richard Kammann; Nature
sources.stance_or_result: Reports failed duplication and argues that cues in transcripts and judging procedures can account for striking matches in earlier work.
sources.limitations: The original authors disputed the interpretation; assess the exchange and exact data rather than citing only one side.
sources.rights_note: Publisher-owned scholarly article. Link by DOI; do not republish the article text.

sources.title: Remote viewing: a response to Marks and Kammann
sources.authors_or_owner: Charles Tart, Harold Puthoff, and Russell Targ; Nature
sources.stance_or_result: Challenges the claim that transcript cues explain the original remote-viewing findings.
sources.limitations: A reply in a disputed exchange; it should not be treated as an independent replication.
sources.rights_note: Publisher-owned scholarly article. Link by DOI; do not republish the article text.

sources.title: Remote viewing
sources.stance_or_result: Critiques the evidential interpretation of remote-viewing experiments and the handling of alternative explanations.
sources.limitations: A short critical contribution, not a comprehensive meta-analysis of the full later literature.
sources.rights_note: Publisher-owned scholarly article. Link by DOI; do not republish the article text.

sources.title: Enhancing Human Performance: Issues, Theories, and Techniques
sources.authors_or_owner: National Research Council, Committee on Techniques for the Enhancement of Human Performance
sources.stance_or_result: The committee reported little or no scientifically supportable evidence for remote viewing and related claimed enhancement techniques in the evidence it reviewed.
sources.limitations: Covers a defined pre-1988 evidence base and multiple enhancement topics; later studies require separate review.
sources.rights_note: National Academies publication. Link to the DOI/read-online record and observe its terms.

sources.title: An Assessment of the Evidence for Psychic Functioning
sources.authors_or_owner: Jessica Utts; prepared for the 1995 AIR evaluation
sources.stance_or_result: Argues that anomalous cognition had been demonstrated under the reviewed laboratory conditions and discusses repeatable statistical effects.
sources.limitations: One commissioned expert interpretation; the conclusion was directly contested by the paired Hyman assessment and does not establish operational usefulness.
sources.rights_note: Link to the later journal reprint/DOI and the official AIR compilation; do not republish the complete article.

sources.title: Evaluation of Program on Anomalous Mental Phenomena
sources.authors_or_owner: Ray Hyman; prepared for the 1995 AIR evaluation
sources.stance_or_result: Acknowledges a statistical anomaly in the better SAIC experiments while arguing that paranormal functioning was not established without independent replication and stronger exclusion of alternatives.
sources.limitations: One commissioned expert interpretation; it does not show that every observed deviation was caused by one identified ordinary artifact.
sources.rights_note: Link to the author-hosted transcription and the official AIR compilation.

sources.title: Remote Viewing: a 1974-2022 systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.authors_or_owner: Patrizio Tressoldi and Alex Katz; Journal of Scientific Exploration
sources.stance_or_result: Reports a positive aggregate effect across the studies meeting the authors' criteria after specified outlier handling.
sources.limitations: The field remains contested; study dependence, publication selection, protocol heterogeneity, scoring, and source-study quality require independent sensitivity analysis.
sources.rights_note: Journal article licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 on the journal page. Link by DOI; preserve author/journal attribution and license terms.

sources.title: Follow-up on the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency's (CIA) remote viewing experiments
sources.authors_or_owner: Álex Escolà-Gascón, James Houran, Neil Dagnall, Kenneth Drinkwater, and Andrew Denovan; Brain and Behavior
sources.stance_or_result: Reports a large quasi-experimental follow-up: one group analysis was nonsignificant, while another group and several subsamples produced significant forced-choice results and associations with experiential emotional intelligence under the authors’ analyses.
sources.limitations: The design was quasi-experimental rather than a randomized replication, group definitions and belief differences matter, the mechanism model is exploratory, and the result requires independent preregistered replication and reanalysis.
sources.rights_note: Open-access Wiley article. Link by DOI and preserve the article-specific license and attribution.

sources.title: Experts’ Remote Viewing Guidelines
sources.authors_or_owner: Akin, Tressoldi, and Katz; Journal of Scientific Exploration
sources.stance_or_result: Reports areas of provisional agreement among eleven experienced remote-viewing practitioners or researchers, including blinding, training, neutral conditions, and the potential value of multiple viewers, while retaining disagreements.
sources.limitations: Expert opinion and consensus mapping are not randomized evidence that the recommended elements improve accuracy.
sources.rights_note: Journal article licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 on the journal page. Link by DOI; preserve author/journal attribution and license terms.
